title: Shorts Bot Operations Graph V1 - Incident Record
description: One structured, evidence-backed record of a real production/CI incident: failure -> root cause -> fix -> regression -> PR -> verification. A summary field is never authority by itself -- every VERIFIED claim must carry GitHub-native evidence (run/job IDs, commit SHAs, PR numbers, test files). See operations/README.md for the full policy.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 date (or date-time) of the failure itself, not the date the record was written. Use the earliest real evidence timestamp (e.g. the first failing run's created_at date).

authority_main_sha.description: The `main` HEAD SHA that was authoritative when this incident was investigated/fixed. null only if genuinely never established (confidence must then be UNVERIFIED or PARTIAL, never VERIFIED).

workflow.description: GitHub Actions workflow file name (e.g. hook_experiment_e2e.yml), or null if not workflow-specific.

run_id.description: GitHub Actions run ID of the failing (or representative) run. null if not captured -- then confidence MUST NOT be VERIFIED.

job_id.description: GitHub Actions job ID within run_id. null if not captured at job granularity.

failure_stage.description: Controlled vocabulary for where in the pipeline the failure surfaced.

failure_signature.description: Short, deterministic fingerprint of the failure -- an exact exception type+message pattern, assertion text, or check name. Used for exact/substring query matching. Must be specific enough to distinguish this incident from an unrelated one with a similar symptom.

symptoms.description: Human-readable observed symptoms (log lines, check names, behavior). Not authority by itself -- root_cause.evidence carries the proof.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what was actually wrong, in evidence-backed terms, not speculation.

evidence.description: GitHub-native evidence supporting the summary. Empty only when confidence is UNVERIFIED.

affected_files.description: Repo-relative paths touched by the root cause and/or the fix.

commits.description: Commit SHAs that make up the fix. Empty only when status is OPEN/MONITORING or confidence is not VERIFIED.

summary.description: What the fix actually does, in concrete terms (not 'fixed the bug').

test_files.description: Repo-relative test file paths that cover this incident.

counterexample.description: Name/id of the specific test case reproducing the original failure, or null if none was added (must be explained in fix.summary why).

result.description: Outcome of running the regression at verification time.

pull_requests.description: PRs that landed (or attempted to land) this fix.

workflow_runs.description: GitHub Actions runs that verified the fix (post-fix green run for the originally-failing check).

verified_sha.description: The exact commit SHA verification ran against.

relationships.description: Edges to other incidents. Controlled vocabulary only.

confidence.description: Evidence completeness, not an agent's subjective certainty. See operations/README.md for the exact VERIFIED/PARTIAL/UNVERIFIED gate rules enforced by operations/validate.py.
